chapter_title: 第66章 開學考的意義

segments.title: 第66章 開學考的意義
segments.content:
Reburning the Verdant Era Chapter 66: The Meaning of the Start-of-Term Exam

Parents seem to have a special ability.

No matter what topic they were originally discussing, they can always inexplicably steer the conversation back to academics.

If it's after college graduation, the conversation will veer towards blind dates or marriage.

If you're married, it will veer towards having children.

All in all, conversations at the dinner table basically revolve around these few things.

"I heard from Xixi that your school is having a start-of-term exam tomorrow?" Halfway through dinner, Lin Xiuhong suddenly asked, "Have you been reviewing well recently?"

"No," Li Luo answered with great honesty.

"...How can you be so brazen about it?"

"We've been having military training."

"What about Xixi then?"

"She reviewed."

"See?" Lin Xiuhong pointed her finger. "How come she reviewed, and you didn't?"

Well, there it was... Mom's old habit again.

Lin Xiuhong was great in every other way, except for this "other people's kids" superpower of hers, which always managed to accurately hit Li Luo's sore spot.

If it weren't for the fact that Li Luo had been reborn from the age of 35 and was now immune to his mom's tactic, the 15-year-old Li Luo would have probably snorted and started giving her the cold shoulder by now.

"Mom, this is where you're mistaken," Li Luo said with a serious face. "Do you know what the start-of-term exam is for?"

"Hmm?" Lin Xiuhong was taken aback by his question, then said, "Isn't it to see if you all studied during summer break?"

"NO, NO, NO." Li Luo raised an index finger, wagging it gently as he said seriously, "The start-of-term exam is for exposing problems and filling in the gaps."

"What do you mean?"

"Think about it, Mom." Li Luo guided her patiently. "For exams like the finals or the high school entrance exam, we all cram like crazy beforehand, a last-minute effort."

"Maybe you get lucky and there's a question on the test that you happened to have practiced, so you get it right."

"But in reality, you haven't truly mastered the principles and knowledge contained in that question. Give it a week or two, and if you're asked to do it again, you might not be able to."

"This shows that even though you got the points, you didn't really grasp the knowledge. It's a false gain."

Lin Xiuhong was stunned by his words. "And then?"

"And then there's the start-of-term exam," Li Luo said with utmost gravity. "If you study hard for it like you would for a final and get a good score..."

"You still haven't truly grasped the knowledge you memorized at the last minute. And because you got it right again, you failed to notice this problem."

"This way, you might not get those points next time if your luck runs out, because you never really mastered it."

"The purpose of the start-of-term exam is to let you rest well during the summer break, so that without much review, your weaknesses are fully exposed."

"Only the knowledge that you have truly absorbed can be used freely and effortlessly, even without reviewing."

"And the questions you get wrong are the gaps you need to fill, the weaknesses you need to work on."

Lin Xiuhong was a bit dazed by his explanation, wondering if there was actually some truth to it.

After all, she had never attended high school herself, so perhaps Li Luo's explanation was correct.

So, Lin Xiuhong turned her head and looked at the girls, hoping to get an answer from them.

"Ahem..." Xu Youyu suppressed a laugh and nodded repeatedly, "What Li Luo said does make a lot of sense."

After all, Xu Youyu hadn't reviewed much herself either... Recently, spurred on by Li Luo's 250,000-word manuscript, she had been writing frantically.

As of today, she had already saved up 20,000 words!

What time did she have for reviewing?

"You still have to do well on the test, you hear?" Lin Xiuhong sighed, feeling like she couldn't quite win an argument with her son now that he was older. "You were 86th in the entire district for the high school entrance exam. That should be pretty high up in your class, right?"

"That was just an exceptional performance on the entrance exam," Li Luo said, managing expectations beforehand. "I can't possibly score that well every time."

"My expectations for you aren't that high then." Lin Xiuhong, unable to do anything about him, could only remind him, "Just don't be at the bottom of the class. You're the class president, aren't you? You can't embarrass yourself academically."

"I know." Li Luo picked up his chopsticks and put a piece of meat in Lin Xiuhong's bowl. "Mom, you should eat more."

After the meal, Ying Chanxi walked Qiao Xinyan home.

Lin Xiufeng also got up to leave.

Lin Xiuhong cleared the table and went to the kitchen to wash the dishes, while Li Luo ambled back to his bedroom.

Just then, Li Guohong followed him into the bedroom, glanced at his computer, and then asked, "I've read that novel of yours."

"Huh?" Startled by the sudden statement, Li Luo practically jumped. "Dad, what did you say?"

"I said I read that novel of yours." Li Guohong sat on the edge of the bed, took out his phone, and said with a smile, "It's quite interesting. I don't know how that head of yours came up with something like this."

"Like the college life you wrote about, how singers release songs, how they compete on the charts, the rivalries between companies."

"It seems quite convincing, but you're just a high school kid. Where did you learn all this stuff?"

"Ahem..." Li Luo got goosebumps from his words. "I learned it all online."

"Your mom recommended it to your uncle before," Li Guohong reminded him. "But your uncle isn't very good with smartphones and can't really use a computer either, so I don't know if he read it or not."

It's best if he didn't!

Li Luo gritted his teeth, feeling like he was about to morph into the very embodiment of embarrassment.

"Your mom and I are on the same page," Li Guohong said. "We don't mind you having this as a hobby, but it can't affect your studies, you understand?"

"Don't worry, I know my limits."

"That's good." Li Guohong chuckled twice, then sighed. "You're a high school student now. Your mom never went to high school, and I went to a vocational high school. Vocational high schools were actually pretty good back then, you know?"

"But now that you're in high school, your mom and I can't really help you much. We don't know anything about getting into college."

"If you have any questions, you must ask your teachers. Don't be afraid of feeling embarrassed."

Hearing his dad's sudden heartfelt words, Li Luo fell silent for a moment.

"Dad."

"Hmm?"

"Is running the breakfast shop tiring?"

"Why are you suddenly asking about that?"

"When I make a lot of money in the future," Li Luo said, "you and Mom can just rest. I'll support you."

"You little rascal." Li Guohong was amused by his words, but his eyes showed deep gratification.

He stood up, walked over to Li Luo, and patted his shoulder. "Your dad is still strong. Your job right now is to study hard. You'll have plenty of opportunities to make money in the future."

Li Luo pursed his lips, wanting to say more, but in the end, he just nodded and gave a firm "Mhm."

Over half an hour later, Lin Xiuhong and Li Guohong finished washing the dishes in the kitchen, tidied up the entire house, and then took their leave.

"Should we review today?"

Ying Chanxi, who had just finished her shower, pushed open the door to Li Luo's bedroom and poked her head in to ask.

"Mhm." Li Luo nodded, turned off his computer, stood up, and walked out of the bedroom to the desk in the living room. "I'll have to trouble you again today."

"Can I join?" Xu Youyu poked her head out of the study and asked with a grin, "You guys don't mind, do you?"

"Senior, sit here." Ying Chanxi sat in the middle of the desk, had Li Luo sit to her left, and offered the spot on her right to Xu Youyu.

"Coming, coming."
